answer: The official Vite light/dark SVGs (introduced by #21339) can render inconsistently in WebKit at small icon sizes (~24px height), showing blurriness, color bleeding around the lightning mark, dark edges, and incorrect interpolation around transparent regions; Chrome renders them correctly [2]. answer: This is a confirmed bug: `optimizeDeps.include` resolves and pre-bundles a project source file, but the dev optimizer resolver only checked optimized metadata for bare specifiers, so a relative import continued through the normal source-file path and never referenced the generated pre-bundle, leaving that output unused [1]. The cause is structural: in `vite:resolve` (and `vite:pre-alias`) the call to `tryOptimizedResolve` sits behind `if (bareImportRE.test(id))`, and `tryOptimizedResolve` matches the optimizer metadata by specifier string, not by resolved file path [4]. Note that a maintainer considers `optimizeDeps` documented to work on deps only, with no plans to make it work for normal files, though a simple guard PR could be considered [3]; the experimental `bundledDev` feature is meant to address the many-project-files problem [3].

Status: sapphi-red says this was "kind of fixed" by rolldown/rolldown#10837 in Rolldown v1.2.8, since `hotUpdate` is now not called temporarily [2]. A narrow fix for the missing `this.environment` binding was opened as #23317, scoped to wrapping `hotUpdate` inside `injectEnvironmentToHooks` (not the broader adapter work in #22956), with a unit test asserting `this.environment.name` is set [3]. The issue reporter's preferred interim behavior is to bind the environment for `hotUpdate` when plugins are handed to the full-bundle dev engine, or else skip `hotUpdate` hooks entirely under bundled dev with a one-time warning naming the plugin [5].

The issue is that in Vite 8, a non-eager `import.meta.glob` call no longer causes the matched files to be included in the build or the manifest, whereas in Vite 7 they were [3][4]. This breaks Laravel apps that relied on `import.meta.glob(['../images/**', '../fonts/**'])` in `app.js` to have unreferenced assets processed and versioned for `Vite::asset()` [3][4]. The reporter notes Vite 8 emits `/* #__PURE__ */` when converting globs, e.g. `/* #__PURE__ */ Object.assign({"../favicons/favicon.ico": () => import("../favicons/favicon.ico")})` [3]. Making the glob eager restores the behavior [1][3]:

```js
import.meta.glob(["../favicons/**"], { eager: true });
```

The Laravel plugin maintainers plan to add an `assets` config key that runs the glob inside the plugin and attach it as an input, and to push users to migrate to that approach in the upgrade guide [2][5]. The excerpts do not state whether Vite will change this behavior to avoid the silent breaking change.

The regression is that `import.meta.glob` with extglobs (e.g. `"./!(stories|types|Common|lib|const|admin-ui)/*!(spec|test|stories).tsx"`) no longer splits code in Vite 8.0.0 the way it did in 7.3.1: the "Before" build produced separate chunks like `Bar-CPzg7Oye.js` and `NotFound-Ck_3-kbz.js`, while the "After" build emits only a single `index-DFpg94Xo.js` [2]. A maintainer confirmed extglob support is the cause and that it's tracked separately at issue #21947 [4].

The workaround is to use an array of globs with negations instead of extglobs [4]:

```ts
import.meta.glob([
  "./**/*.tsx",
  "!./{stories,types,Common,lib,const,admin-ui}/**/*.tsx",
  "!./**/*.{spec,test,stories}.tsx",
])
```

Note that `**` matches any nesting depth, so if you need exactly one level deep (`category/name.tsx`), use `"./*/*.tsx"` with the same negations, as the reporter confirmed works [1][3].
